translations.title: US Return Address For Mexican Sellers: Handling Northbound Returns
translations.excerpt: A Mexican seller reaching US customers hits the same wall in reverse: without a US return address, every return becomes an export and the cost usually exceeds the product.
translations.content:
A Mexican seller selling to US customers needs a return address inside the United States. Without one, each return is an international shipment whose cost usually exceeds the value of the product. With one, the return is a domestic parcel, the unit can be inspected and restocked in the US, and only the small share worth recovering travels south consolidated.

  • US buyers expect a domestic return address and compare your policy against local sellers.
  • Without a US address, each return becomes an international shipment with its own formalities and cost.
  • Returned units in resellable condition can go straight back into US sellable stock rather than crossing the border twice.
  • Only the minority of units genuinely worth recovering should travel south, and they should travel consolidated.
  • A well documented truck covers Monterrey to Laredo in one to two business days (operational data).

How do Mexican sellers handle returns from US customers?

By having an address inside the United States that receives them. It does not need to be your own facility. What matters is that the buyer ships domestically and that someone inspects the unit before deciding what happens to it.

A Mexican company selling into the United States runs into the mirror image of the problem US sellers face going south, and it is worth stating plainly because the solution is the same shape. Your US customer expects to return the way they return to any local store: print a label, drop the parcel, get refunded. If your only return address is in Mexico, that is not what happens. The parcel becomes an international shipment, it needs documentation, it moves at international speed, and the cost of moving one item is wildly out of proportion to the item itself. In most consumer categories the return shipping alone exceeds the product value, which pushes sellers into two bad habits: refusing returns, which damages the listing and invites disputes, or refunding without recovering the goods, which means eating the full cost of every return. The third option is an address inside the United States. It does not have to be a facility you own; a logistics partner operating there provides the same thing. The customer ships domestically, which is fast and cheap for them, the parcel arrives in days rather than weeks, and you get the thing that actually matters: possession of the unit and the ability to inspect it before deciding what it is worth. That single change turns returns from a fixed loss into a recovery process.

What to do with the unit once it arrives

Log it against the order, grade it, then send it down one of three paths: back into US sellable stock, into a secondary channel, or disposal. Sending it back to Mexico should be the exception, and when it happens it should be consolidated.

A return address is just a mailbox until there is a process behind it, and the process is short. Step one is intake: record what arrived and match it to an order, because an unmatched return is a refund dispute waiting to happen. Step two is inspection and grading, sorting units honestly into condition tiers rather than treating them as one pile. From there, three paths. Units in resellable condition go straight back into your US inventory and sell again to the next US customer. This is the path that makes the whole model pay, because the unit becomes revenue without crossing any border in either direction. Units with damaged packaging or light wear go to a secondary channel, which depending on your category might be a discounted listing, a refurbished offer or a bundle. Units that are genuinely unsellable go to disposal, and it is worth being decisive here rather than paying to store things that will never sell. Only after this sorting does sending anything to Mexico make sense. Usually the answer is that a minority of units justify it, and when they do they should travel together in one consolidated shipment rather than one at a time. A well documented truck covers Monterrey to Laredo in one to two business days, so batching costs you very little time and saves a great deal of money.

Setting it up, and the second thing it buys you

Decide who receives, publish a clear English return policy, write down grading rules, and set a consolidation rhythm. The same US facility that handles returns also serves as the forward stocking point that makes your US delivery times competitive.

Four decisions get this running. First, who receives the returns. Very few Mexican sellers need their own US facility for this, because returns volume is a fraction of outbound volume and a lease plus staff rarely pays for itself; most use a partner already operating there. Second, what the customer sees: a return policy in English, easy to find, specific about the window, the condition expected and how the refund is issued. Vague policies generate support tickets and chargebacks rather than clean returns. Third, the grading rulebook, written before the first return arrives so the decision does not depend on who opens the box. Fourth, the consolidation rhythm, meaning how often the small number of recoverable units travel south. Then there is a second benefit that often matters more than the returns themselves. The same US facility that receives returns can hold forward stock for US orders. Once you have inventory sitting in the United States, your US delivery times stop being international and start being domestic, which is the single biggest factor in whether a US buyer chooses you over a local seller. In other words, the infrastructure you build to stop losing money on returns is the same infrastructure that lets you compete properly in that market. BringGo Ship runs warehouses in Laredo and Monterrey, so a US return point, inspection, restocking and consolidated southbound shipments sit in one chain.

What the return isInternational shipmentDomestic parcel
Cost per returnOften exceeds product valueLocal parcel rate
SpeedWeeksDays
Resellable unitsCross the border twiceBack into US stock

Extra benefitNoneSame facility holds forward US stock

Definitions

  • Northbound return: A northbound return is a product sent back by a US customer to a seller based in Mexico.
  • Grading: Grading is sorting returned units by condition so each follows the right path: restock, secondary channel or disposal.
  • Forward stock: Forward stock is inventory held inside the destination market so orders ship domestically rather than internationally.

Frequently asked questions

Do Mexican sellers need a US return address?

In practice yes, if you sell to US consumers. Buyers expect to return the way they do to any local store. Without a US address each return is an international shipment whose cost usually exceeds the product value, which pushes sellers into refusing returns or refunding without recovering the goods.

Does the return address have to be my own facility?

No. Returns volume is normally a fraction of outbound volume, so a lease and staff rarely pay for themselves. Most Mexican sellers use a logistics partner already operating in the United States. What matters is that the buyer ships domestically and that someone inspects the unit before deciding what it is worth.

What happens to returned units that are still good?

They go straight back into your US sellable stock and sell again to the next US customer. This is the path that makes the model pay, because the unit becomes revenue without crossing any border in either direction. Sending it home to Mexico would mean paying to move it twice for no gain.

Should I ship returns back to Mexico?

Only the minority where recovered value clearly justifies it, and then consolidated rather than one at a time. A well documented truck covers Monterrey to Laredo in one to two business days, so batching costs very little time and saves a great deal of money compared with individual shipments.

Is there any benefit beyond cheaper returns?

Yes, and it is often bigger. The same US facility can hold forward stock for US orders. Once inventory sits in the United States your delivery times stop being international and become domestic, which is the main factor in whether a US buyer chooses you over a local seller.

translations.title: Restricción Horaria Para Tráileres En Monterrey: Cómo Planear Entregas
translations.excerpt: Tu carga puede llegar a tiempo a Monterrey y aun así no poder entregarse. La restricción de circulación es municipal y cambia, y planear sin conocerla cuesta un día.
translations.content:
En la zona metropolitana de Monterrey la circulación de vehículos de carga pesada está regulada a nivel municipal, con horarios y rutas que varían entre municipios y que se actualizan. La consecuencia práctica es que una carga puede llegar a tiempo y aun así no poder entregarse hasta la siguiente ventana permitida, así que la entrega se programa contra el horario local y no solo contra el tránsito.

  • La circulación de carga pesada en la zona metro de Monterrey se regula por municipio, no por una sola norma estatal uniforme.
  • Los horarios y rutas permitidas cambian, por lo que deben confirmarse con el transportista antes de programar la entrega.
  • Una carga puede llegar dentro del tiempo de tránsito y aun así esperar a la siguiente ventana permitida para entregar.
  • Un camión bien documentado cubre Laredo a Monterrey en uno o dos días hábiles (dato operativo).
  • Entregar en zonas industriales suele ser más flexible que entregar en zonas urbanas o comerciales densas.

¿A qué horas pueden circular tráileres en Monterrey?

Depende del municipio. La zona metropolitana está formada por varios municipios y cada uno regula la circulación de carga pesada con sus propios horarios y rutas. Por eso no existe una sola respuesta válida para toda el área y hay que confirmarla antes de programar.

Aquí conviene ser honesto en lugar de dar una cifra que suene precisa. La zona metropolitana de Monterrey no es un solo municipio: incluye Monterrey, San Pedro Garza García, Guadalupe, San Nicolás, Apodaca, Escobedo, Santa Catarina y otros, y la circulación de vehículos de carga pesada se regula a nivel municipal. Cada municipio define sus propias restricciones de horario y sus rutas permitidas, y esas disposiciones se actualizan. Publicar aquí un horario fijo sería cómodo pero te induciría al error, porque el horario que aplica a tu entrega depende de en qué municipio está la dirección de destino y de la norma vigente ese mes. Lo que sí podemos decir con seguridad es qué lógica siguen estas restricciones, porque es consistente. Buscan sacar los vehículos pesados de las vías urbanas en las horas de mayor congestión, proteger ciertas zonas residenciales, comerciales y escolares, y canalizar la carga por corredores diseñados para soportarla. De ahí se derivan tres implicaciones prácticas: las ventanas de entrega tienden a abrirse fuera de las horas pico, las zonas industriales suelen ser más flexibles que las urbanas densas, y el tipo de vehículo importa, porque lo que se restringe casi siempre son las unidades de mayor tamaño y peso.

Por qué esto cambia tu planeación, no solo tu ruta

Porque el tiempo de tránsito y la hora de entrega son cosas distintas. Un camión puede llegar en el plazo previsto y aun así esperar a la siguiente ventana permitida, y esa espera se convierte en un día perdido si nadie la contempló.

El error más común no es incumplir la norma, es planear como si no existiera. Un camión bien documentado cubre Laredo a Monterrey en uno o dos días hábiles, y esa cifra es real, pero describe el tránsito, no la entrega. Si la unidad llega a la zona metropolitana fuera de la ventana permitida para su tipo de vehículo en ese municipio, no entrega: espera. Y una espera de unas horas suele convertirse en un día completo, porque el destinatario también tiene horario de recepción. Cuando ese día no estaba contemplado, aparece como retraso del transportista aunque nadie haya hecho nada mal. La segunda consecuencia es sobre el tipo de unidad. Si tu destino final está en una zona con restricción fuerte, mover la carga hasta ahí en un tráiler completo puede ser inviable, y la solución operativa es transferir a una unidad más pequeña en un punto intermedio. Eso es una decisión de diseño de red, no una improvisación del día de la entrega: implica un punto donde hacer la transferencia y un costo adicional que debe estar en la cotización desde el inicio. La tercera consecuencia es sobre las citas. En destinos con ventana estrecha, la cita de entrega deja de ser un trámite y pasa a ser el eje de la programación: primero se consigue la cita, después se planea el cruce.

Qué preguntar antes de programar

Pregunta el municipio del destino, si aplica restricción a tu tipo de unidad, cuál es la ventana permitida hoy, si el destino tiene horario de recepción propio y si hará falta transferir a una unidad menor. Cinco preguntas antes de cotizar, no después.

La forma de no perder días es convertir esto en cinco preguntas que se hacen antes de cerrar la operación. Primera: ¿en qué municipio está exactamente la dirección de entrega? No basta con decir Monterrey, porque la zona metropolitana abarca varios municipios con reglas distintas. Segunda: ¿aplica restricción de circulación al tipo de unidad que va a llevar mi carga? Lo que se restringe suele ser el tamaño y el peso, así que la respuesta cambia según si va en tráiler completo o en unidad menor. Tercera: ¿cuál es la ventana permitida vigente para ese municipio? Vigente es la palabra clave, porque estas disposiciones se actualizan y una referencia del año pasado puede estar desfasada; tu transportista local es quien tiene el dato actual. Cuarta: ¿el destino tiene su propio horario de recepción y requiere cita? En muchos casos esa ventana es más estrecha que la municipal y termina siendo la restricción que manda. Quinta: ¿va a hacer falta transferir a una unidad más pequeña, y ese costo está en la cotización? Si la respuesta es sí y no estaba cotizado, aparecerá como cargo extra al final. Un operador que trabaja el corredor a diario responde estas cinco sin dudar, y esa es una buena forma de distinguir a quien conoce la ciudad de quien solo mueve carga hasta la frontera. BringGo Ship opera bodegas en Laredo y Monterrey, de modo que el cruce, la entrega local y la programación se planean juntos.

Tipo de unidadSe restringe tamaño y pesoTu transportista
Ventana permitida vigenteLas disposiciones se actualizanTransportista local

Definiciones

  • Ventana de entrega: La ventana de entrega es el rango horario en el que un vehículo de carga puede circular y entregar en un municipio determinado.
  • Transferencia a unidad menor: Es pasar la carga de un tráiler a un vehículo más pequeño en un punto intermedio para poder entrar a zonas con restricción.
  • Zona metropolitana de Monterrey: Es el conjunto de municipios alrededor de Monterrey, cada uno con su propia regulación de circulación de carga.

Preguntas frecuentes

¿A qué horas pueden circular tráileres en Monterrey?

Depende del municipio. La zona metropolitana incluye varios municipios y cada uno regula la circulación de carga pesada con sus propios horarios y rutas, que además se actualizan. No existe una sola respuesta válida para toda el área, así que hay que confirmarla con el transportista antes de programar.

¿Por qué mi carga llegó a tiempo y no se entregó?

Porque el tiempo de tránsito y la hora de entrega son cosas distintas. Si la unidad llega fuera de la ventana permitida para su tipo de vehículo en ese municipio, espera a la siguiente. Una espera de horas suele convertirse en un día completo, porque el destinatario también tiene horario de recepción.

¿Qué lógica siguen estas restricciones?

Sacar los vehículos pesados de las vías urbanas en horas de mayor congestión, proteger zonas residenciales, comerciales y escolares, y canalizar la carga por corredores diseñados para soportarla. Por eso las zonas industriales suelen ser más flexibles que las zonas urbanas densas.

¿Voy a necesitar cambiar a un camión más pequeño?

Es posible si el destino está en una zona con restricción fuerte. La solución operativa es transferir la carga a una unidad menor en un punto intermedio. Eso implica un punto de transferencia y un costo adicional, y debe estar en la cotización desde el inicio para que no aparezca como cargo extra al final.

¿Qué debo preguntar antes de programar una entrega?

El municipio exacto del destino, si aplica restricción a tu tipo de unidad, cuál es la ventana permitida vigente, si el destinatario tiene su propio horario de recepción y si hará falta transferir a una unidad menor con su costo. Un operador que trabaja el corredor a diario responde las cinco sin dudar.

translations.title: Do Trucks Get Inspected When Crossing Into Mexico?
translations.excerpt: Mexican customs does not inspect every truck, and it does not choose at random in the way most shippers assume. Understanding the selection mechanism tells you what you can and cannot control.
translations.content:
Not every truck is inspected. Mexico uses an automated selection mechanism at clearance that designates a portion of shipments for reconocimiento aduanero, a physical and documentary examination. Shipments not selected are released without examination. Selection is partly randomised and partly risk-based, so importers with clean classification, consistent values and complete documentation face both fewer examinations and much shorter ones when selected.

  • Mexico's clearance process runs an automated selection mechanism that determines whether a shipment receives reconocimiento aduanero.
  • Reconocimiento aduanero covers both the physical goods and the documentation, checking that what arrived matches what was declared.
  • Selection is not purely random; risk profiling considers importer history, product category, declared value and origin.
  • A shipment that matches its declaration clears examination quickly; discrepancies trigger sampling, valuation review or seizure.
  • From 1 August 2026, an incomplete electronic Manifestación de Valor is itself a documentary problem, since the filing became mandatory through the single window.

How does Mexico decide which trucks to inspect?

An automated selection mechanism runs at clearance and designates a share of shipments for examination, combining randomisation with risk profiling.

When your customs broker files the pedimento and the shipment is presented, an automated system determines whether the shipment proceeds directly or goes to reconocimiento aduanero. This is not a customs officer deciding on sight. The randomised component means that even a perfectly compliant importer will occasionally be selected. You cannot engineer your way out of it, and you should not try. The risk-profiling component is where your behaviour matters: importer history, the product category, the declared value relative to what customs expects for that classification, and the origin of the goods all feed the profile. The practical implication is that an importer's inspection rate is not fixed. A first-time importer bringing in a category that is commonly undervalued will see more examinations than an established importer with a consistent record in a low-risk category. That record is built over time and it is an asset worth protecting.

What happens during an inspection?

Officials verify that the physical goods match the declaration: quantity, description, classification, and value support.

An examination checks correspondence. The officer compares the goods against the pedimento, the commercial invoice and the packing list. Quantity, description, and whether the classification fits the goods as they actually are. Most examinations that go badly go badly for mundane reasons. Cartons contain more units than the packing list says. The invoice describes 'electronic accessories' and the carton contains something with a specific regulatory requirement. The declared value is far below what the classification usually carries and there is no documentation supporting why. When a discrepancy appears, the consequences scale with the type. A minor documentary error may be corrected through a pedimento rectification with a fee and a delay. A valuation dispute opens a review that can hold the shipment for an extended period. A regulatory violation, such as goods requiring COFEPRIS authorisation or NOM certification that were declared as something else, can result in seizure. The shipments that clear examination fastest are the boring ones: what was declared is what is in the trailer.

What can a shipper actually control?

Classification accuracy, description precision, value documentation and completeness of the file. Not selection itself.

Start with classification, because it determines everything downstream. The HS code decides the duty rate, whether a permit or NOM certification applies, and what the customs system expects the value to look like. Getting it wrong does not just cost duty; it can put you in a category where you had no idea a permit was required. Write descriptions that a person can verify by opening a box. 'Cotton t-shirts, men's, short sleeve, 180gsm' is verifiable. 'Apparel' is not, and it invites questions. Keep value documentation with the file, not in someone's inbox. Purchase orders, payment records and price lists supporting the declared transaction value should be retrievable while the truck is at the border, not a week later. And make sure the Manifestación de Valor is filed electronically. Since 1 August 2026 this is mandatory through the single window that ANAM's 2026 communications call VUTCE, the successor to VUCEM. A missing value manifest converts a routine examination into a documentary failure. What you cannot control is selection. Build a schedule that tolerates an occasional examination rather than one that assumes every shipment sails through.

What determines examination outcome

FactorUnder your controlEffect if wrong
Selection for examinationNoAdds time regardless of compliance
HS classificationYesWrong duty, missed permits, valuation flags
Goods descriptionYesQuestioning, sampling, delay
Value documentationYesValuation review, extended hold
Electronic value manifestYesDocumentary non-compliance since 1 August 2026

Definitions

  • Reconocimiento aduanero: Reconocimiento aduanero is the physical and documentary examination of a shipment carried out when the automated selection mechanism designates it.
  • Pedimento rectification: A pedimento rectification is a formal correction to a filed customs declaration, which carries a fee and typically delays release.

Frequently asked questions

Are all trucks inspected at the Mexican border?

No. An automated selection mechanism designates a portion of shipments for reconocimiento aduanero. Shipments not selected are released without physical examination.

Can I avoid being selected for inspection?

No, because selection includes a randomised component. You can reduce your risk profile through accurate classification, precise descriptions and a consistent import history, but no importer is exempt.

How long does a customs examination take?

A shipment that matches its declaration is typically released the same day. Discrepancies extend this considerably: valuation reviews and regulatory issues can hold goods for a week or longer.

What is the most common reason inspections go wrong?

Mismatch between the declaration and the goods. Quantity differences, vague descriptions that hide a regulated product, and declared values without supporting documentation are the recurring causes.

translations.title: Amazon Mexico Tax Withholding For Foreign Sellers: IVA And ISR Explained
translations.excerpt: Selling on Amazon Mexico without a Mexican tax registration is not just a compliance gap. It is a direct and immediate hit to your cash flow, applied to every order.
translations.content:
Amazon Mexico withholds tax from marketplace sellers at source. A seller who has not provided a valid Mexican RFC faces the maximum rates: 20 percent ISR on the sale price and the full 16 percent IVA. Sellers with a registered RFC face substantially lower ISR withholding, and registered taxpayers can credit withheld IVA against their own liability. The withholding is applied by Amazon and remitted to SAT; it is not optional and it is not negotiable.

  • Without a valid RFC, ISR withholding is 20 percent of the sale price, applied regardless of your actual margin.
  • Without an RFC, or where funds are paid to a foreign bank account, platforms withhold 100 percent of the IVA, which at the standard rate means 16 percent.
  • Mexico's 2026 tax framework extended automatic withholding across digital platforms including Amazon and Mercado Libre, for both individuals and companies.
  • IVA withheld from a registered taxpayer can be credited; IVA withheld from an unregistered foreign seller generally cannot be recovered.
  • Withholding is calculated on the sale price, not on profit, which is why it hits low-margin categories hardest.

What does Amazon withhold and at what rate?

Two separate taxes. ISR at 20 percent of the sale price for sellers without an RFC, and IVA at the full 16 percent where no RFC is provided or funds go to a foreign account.

Mexico requires digital platforms to withhold tax at source from the sellers who trade on them. Amazon does not choose to do this; it is a legal obligation, and the amount depends on what you have told Amazon about your tax status. ISR is income tax. For a seller without a valid RFC the withholding is 20 percent of the sale price. Read that carefully: the sale price, not the profit. A seller running a 15 percent margin does not pay 20 percent of the margin, they lose more than the margin itself on that transaction. IVA is value added tax, standard rate 16 percent. Where the seller has not provided an RFC, or where proceeds are paid to a foreign bank account, the platform withholds the entire IVA rather than a partial share. The two stack. A seller without an RFC selling into Mexico sees both applied to the same transaction, and the combined effect is severe enough that many sellers discover their Mexico operation was never profitable once the first settlement report arrives.

Why does the RFC change the outcome so much?

The maximum rates function as a default for unidentified taxpayers. Registration moves you into the ordinary regime with lower rates and recoverable IVA.

The high withholding is not a penalty in the formal sense, but it works like one. Mexico's tax authority cannot assess a seller it cannot identify, so the system withholds at the top of the range and leaves it to the seller to register and reconcile. Once you have a valid RFC and the platform has it on file, two things change. ISR withholding falls to the rate applicable to your regime rather than the punitive default. And withheld IVA becomes creditable: as a registered taxpayer you offset it against the IVA you charge and owe, so it stops being a permanent cost and becomes a timing difference. For a foreign seller without Mexican registration, withheld IVA is generally not recoverable. That is the part sellers underestimate. The ISR is painful but visible; the unrecoverable IVA is a silent 16 percent that never comes back. This is why the RFC question is not a paperwork preference. It determines whether roughly a third of your revenue is a tax cost or a recoverable balance.

What are the options for a foreign seller?

Register a Mexican entity and obtain an RFC, work through a structure that holds the RFC, or accept the maximum withholding as a cost of doing business.

Establishing a Mexican entity gives you an RFC, access to the ordinary tax regime, creditable IVA and the ability to enrol in the padrón de importadores so you can import in your own name. The cost is time, professional fees and ongoing filing obligations, including monthly returns whether or not you traded. Operating through a structure that holds the Mexican tax registration is what many cross-border sellers use, particularly when combined with an importer of record arrangement. It resolves the import side and the tax registration together. It is a real commercial relationship, so understand who bears which liability before signing. Accepting the withholding is a legitimate short-term choice while you test the market, provided you price for it. What does not work is pricing as though the withholding is not there and hoping to fix it later. The withholding applies from your first order. Whichever route you choose, model it before you launch. Take a representative SKU, apply 20 percent ISR and 16 percent IVA to the sale price, subtract landed cost and Amazon's referral and fulfilment fees, and see what remains. That number, not the gross margin, is your Mexico business case.

Withholding by seller status

Seller statusISR withholdingIVA treatment
No RFC provided20 percent of sale priceFull 16 percent withheld, generally not recoverable
Proceeds to foreign bank accountApplies per regimeFull IVA withheld
Valid RFC, registered regimeRate per applicable regimeWithheld IVA creditable against liability

Definitions

  • RFC: The RFC (Registro Federal de Contribuyentes) is the Mexican tax identification number required for tax registration, importing and reduced platform withholding.
  • ISR: ISR (Impuesto Sobre la Renta) is Mexican income tax, withheld by marketplaces from seller proceeds at a rate that depends on the seller's registration status.
  • IVA: IVA (Impuesto al Valor Agregado) is Mexican value added tax at a standard rate of 16 percent, creditable by registered taxpayers and a sunk cost for unregistered foreign sellers.

Frequently asked questions

How much does Amazon Mexico withhold if I have no RFC?

20 percent ISR on the sale price plus the full 16 percent IVA. Both are calculated on the sale price rather than on profit, which is why the combined effect often exceeds a seller's gross margin.

Can I get the withheld IVA back?

A registered Mexican taxpayer can credit withheld IVA against IVA owed. A foreign seller without Mexican tax registration generally cannot recover it, so it becomes a permanent cost.

Do I need a Mexican company to get an RFC?

In practice, tax registration in Mexico requires either a Mexican legal entity or an individual with Mexican tax residency. Foreign sellers commonly work through a structure that holds the registration instead.

Is the withholding calculated on profit or on the sale price?

On the sale price. This is the detail that surprises most sellers, because a 20 percent withholding on revenue can exceed the entire margin on a low-margin product.

Does providing a bank account in Mexico change the withholding?

Paying proceeds to a foreign bank account triggers full IVA withholding. A Mexican account alone does not substitute for an RFC, but the combination of RFC and local account produces the ordinary treatment.

translations.title: What Is A Mexico RFC And Do You Need One?
translations.excerpt: The RFC sits underneath almost every Mexican commercial requirement: importing, invoicing, marketplace withholding. Knowing whether you need one is the first structural decision in a Mexico strategy.
translations.content:
The RFC (Registro Federal de Contribuyentes) is Mexico's tax identification number, issued by SAT to individuals and companies with Mexican tax obligations. You need one to enrol in the padrón de importadores and import commercially, to issue CFDI electronic invoices, and to avoid maximum marketplace withholding. A foreign company cannot obtain an RFC without establishing Mexican tax presence, which is why foreign sellers typically work through a structure that holds one.

  • The RFC is issued by SAT and is required for enrolment in the padrón de importadores, without which commercial importing is not possible.
  • Issuing a CFDI, Mexico's mandatory electronic invoice, requires an RFC and an active e.firma.
  • Marketplaces withhold at maximum rates from sellers who have not provided a valid RFC: 20 percent ISR and the full 16 percent IVA.
  • An RFC brings ongoing obligations, including periodic returns that must be filed whether or not there was activity in the period.
  • Enrolment in the padrón de importadores additionally requires a positive opinión de cumplimiento, so outstanding tax issues block the application.

What is the RFC and what does it unlock?

It is Mexico's tax ID, and it is the prerequisite for importing, invoicing, and being treated as an ordinary taxpayer rather than an unidentified one.

The RFC is the identifier SAT uses for every taxpayer in Mexico. Structurally it is similar to a tax identification number elsewhere, but its practical reach in commercial operations is wider than most foreign sellers expect. Three things depend on it. Importing: enrolment in the padrón de importadores requires an RFC, and without padrón enrolment you cannot be the importer of record on a commercial shipment. Invoicing: Mexican business customers require a CFDI, the electronic invoice, to deduct their purchase, and issuing one requires an RFC and a valid e.firma. Withholding: marketplaces apply maximum rates to sellers without an RFC. There is a fourth, less obvious effect. Mexican B2B buyers frequently will not transact with a supplier who cannot issue a CFDI, because the purchase becomes non-deductible for them. This is not a preference; it is an accounting consequence. If your Mexico plan involves selling to businesses, the RFC is not optional in any practical sense.

Can a foreign company get an RFC?

Not without Mexican tax presence. In practice this means a Mexican legal entity, a permanent establishment, or working through a structure that already holds one.

An RFC is issued to taxpayers with Mexican tax obligations. A company incorporated in the United States, Turkey or Spain with no Mexican presence does not have those obligations and cannot simply apply. The routes that do work are three. Incorporating a Mexican entity, typically an S. de R.L. or S.A. de C.V., which then obtains its own RFC. Registering a permanent establishment, which is appropriate in narrower circumstances and carries its own tax consequences. Or contracting with a Mexican entity that acts as importer of record and, where relevant, as the invoicing party. The third is what most cross-border e-commerce sellers use, and it is what Amazon expects when it asks a foreign seller for a FIOR. It is legitimate. It is also a genuine allocation of legal responsibility: the Mexican entity is answerable to SAT and to customs for what is declared under its registration, which is why these arrangements are contractual rather than casual. The wrong approach is to borrow someone's RFC informally. The registration carries liability, and using another party's registration without a proper arrangement exposes both sides.

What does having an RFC oblige you to do?

File periodic returns, maintain a positive compliance opinion, keep the fiscal address current, and hold a valid e.firma.

An RFC is not a one-time registration you obtain and forget. It creates recurring obligations, and the cost of neglecting them shows up at the worst moment. Periodic returns must be filed even for periods with no activity. A dormant entity that stops filing accumulates omissions, and those omissions turn the opinión de cumplimiento negative. That compliance opinion matters more than it sounds. It is required for padrón de importadores enrolment and is checked for various procedures. An importer who lets it lapse can find shipments blocked not because of anything wrong with the shipment, but because a return was missed months earlier. The e.firma, Mexico's advanced electronic signature, must be kept valid. It expires, and renewal requires an appointment. Companies discover this when they need to file something urgently and cannot. The fiscal address must be real and locatable. SAT verifies addresses, and a domicile that cannot be verified can move the taxpayer status to non-localised, which cascades into the compliance opinion. None of this is onerous with a competent Mexican accountant. All of it is expensive to fix retroactively.

Routes to Mexican tax registration

RouteTimelineSuits
Incorporate a Mexican entityMonths, plus ongoing filingsCommitted market entry, own-name importing
Work through an importer of recordDays to weeksE-commerce and marketplace sellers
Sell DDP to a Mexican buyerImmediateB2B where the buyer already has structure

Definitions

  • e.firma: The e.firma is Mexico's advanced electronic signature, required for filing returns, issuing invoices and completing SAT procedures, and it expires and must be renewed.
  • Opinión de cumplimiento: The opinión de cumplimiento is SAT's compliance status certificate, which must be positive for padrón enrolment and various other procedures.
  • CFDI: A CFDI is Mexico's mandatory electronic invoice, which Mexican business buyers require in order to deduct a purchase.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need an RFC to sell on Amazon Mexico?

You can sell without one, but Amazon will withhold at maximum rates: 20 percent ISR and the full 16 percent IVA. Without Mexican tax registration the withheld IVA is generally not recoverable.

Can a US or Turkish company obtain a Mexican RFC?

Not directly. An RFC requires Mexican tax obligations, which means a Mexican entity or permanent establishment. Foreign sellers commonly work through a Mexican entity acting as importer of record instead.

Do I need an RFC to import into Mexico?

Yes. Enrolment in the padrón de importadores requires an RFC, and commercial imports require padrón enrolment. The importer of record must therefore be a Mexican registered taxpayer.

What happens if I have an RFC but stop filing?

Omitted returns turn your opinión de cumplimiento negative, which can block padrón enrolment and other procedures. Returns must be filed even for periods with no activity.

translations.title: FIOR: El Foreign Importer Of Record Que Amazon Te Pide
translations.excerpt: Amazon pide un FIOR y muchos vendedores lo tratan como un dato más del formulario. Es una figura con responsabilidad legal real frente a la aduana mexicana, y conviene entender quién responde por qué.
translations.content:
El FIOR (Foreign Importer of Record) es la figura mediante la cual una entidad mexicana actúa como importador registrado por cuenta de un vendedor extranjero que no tiene presencia fiscal en México. Permite importar sin constituir una empresa mexicana, pero la entidad que funge como importador asume responsabilidad frente a la autoridad aduanera por la exactitud de lo declarado. No es un trámite administrativo: es una relación jurídica con obligaciones reales para ambas partes.

  • Una empresa extranjera no puede ser importador registrado en México; el importador debe tener RFC e inscripción en el padrón de importadores.
  • El FIOR permite operar sin constituir entidad mexicana, pero la responsabilidad aduanera recae en la entidad mexicana que funge como importador.
  • Amazon solicita esta figura a vendedores extranjeros precisamente porque la plataforma no puede ser el importador de la mercancía de terceros.
  • El pedimento se emite a nombre del importador registrado, no del vendedor extranjero.
  • Desde el 1 de agosto de 2026, la Manifestación de Valor que sustenta el valor declarado debe presentarse electrónicamente, y esa obligación corresponde al importador.

¿Qué es exactamente un FIOR?

Una entidad mexicana con RFC y padrón que funge como importador registrado por cuenta de un vendedor extranjero sin presencia fiscal en México.

El punto de partida es una restricción legal: en México el importador registrado tiene que ser un contribuyente mexicano inscrito en el padrón de importadores. Una empresa estadounidense, turca o española sin presencia fiscal en el país no puede serlo. El FIOR resuelve ese problema. Una entidad mexicana con RFC vigente y padrón activo aparece como importador en el pedimento, y la mercancía del vendedor extranjero entra legalmente al país. Lo que conviene entender es qué se transfiere y qué no. La titularidad comercial de la mercancía puede seguir siendo del vendedor extranjero. La responsabilidad aduanera, en cambio, corre por cuenta de la entidad que aparece como importador: es quien responde ante la autoridad por la clasificación arancelaria, el valor declarado, el cumplimiento de regulaciones no arancelarias y la conservación de la documentación. Por eso un FIOR serio pide información detallada antes de aceptar una operación. Si alguien ofrece el servicio sin preguntar qué va dentro de las cajas, esa señal dice más de lo que parece.

¿Por qué Amazon lo exige?

Porque Amazon no importa la mercancía de sus vendedores. Necesita que exista un importador registrado identificable para la mercancía que llega a sus centros.

Cuando un vendedor extranjero manda inventario a un centro de Amazon en México, alguien tiene que haberlo importado. Amazon no asume esa función: recibe y almacena mercancía que ya entró al país legalmente. Por eso la plataforma pide al vendedor extranjero que identifique quién es su importador registrado. No es un requisito interno de Amazon; es el reflejo de la exigencia legal mexicana en el flujo operativo de la plataforma. Esto explica también por qué un vendedor no puede enviar directamente desde Estados Unidos a un centro logístico mexicano sin resolver antes la estructura de importación. La mercancía tiene que despacharse antes de llegar, con pedimento a nombre de un importador registrado. Y conviene ligarlo con el tema fiscal, porque van juntos. El vendedor sin RFC sufre retención de 20 por ciento de ISR y del 16 por ciento de IVA completo sobre sus ventas. Resolver la importación mediante FIOR y no resolver el RFC deja el problema fiscal intacto. Son dos decisiones distintas y ambas tienen que tomarse.

¿Qué debe revisar antes de contratar un FIOR?

Que el padrón esté activo, quién responde ante una revisión, cómo se maneja la documentación de valor y qué pasa con las devoluciones.

Primero, verifique que la entidad tenga padrón de importadores activo y opinión de cumplimiento positiva. Un padrón suspendido detiene sus embarques sin previo aviso y usted se entera cuando la mercancía ya está en la frontera. Segundo, defina por contrato quién responde ante una revisión posterior. La autoridad puede revisar operaciones tiempo después del despacho. Si aparece una diferencia de clasificación o de valor, el importador registrado es el sujeto obligado, pero la relación entre ustedes determina quién absorbe el costo. Eso se pacta antes, no cuando llega el requerimiento. Tercero, aclare el manejo de la documentación de valor. Desde el 1 de agosto de 2026 la Manifestación de Valor debe presentarse electrónicamente por la ventanilla única que la ANAM denomina VUTCE en sus comunicados de 2026. Esa obligación es del importador, y quien la cumple necesita información veraz de usted: facturas, órdenes de compra, evidencia de pago. Si usted no entrega esa información, está pidiéndole a alguien que declare bajo protesta algo que no puede sustentar. Cuarto, resuelva las devoluciones desde el inicio. La mercancía que entra bajo un FIOR y luego se devuelve o se retorna tiene su propio tratamiento aduanero. Es más barato diseñarlo que improvisarlo.

Quién responde por qué en un esquema FIOR

AspectoVendedor extranjeroImportador registrado (FIOR)
Titularidad de la mercancíaNormalmente conservaNo necesariamente
Nombre en el pedimentoNo aparece como importadorAparece como importador
Responsabilidad ante la aduanaIndirecta, vía contratoDirecta
Veracidad de la información de valorDebe proporcionarlaDebe declararla
Manifestación de Valor electrónicaAporta sustentoObligado a presentarla

Definiciones

  • Importador registrado: El importador registrado es la persona inscrita en el padrón de importadores a cuyo nombre se emite el pedimento y que responde ante la autoridad por la operación.
  • Padrón de importadores: El padrón de importadores es el registro del SAT sin el cual no puede realizarse una importación comercial a México.

Preguntas frecuentes

¿Puedo importar a México sin constituir empresa mexicana?

Sí, mediante un esquema de importador registrado como el FIOR, en el que una entidad mexicana con RFC y padrón funge como importador por cuenta de usted. También puede vender DDP a un comprador mexicano que importe en su nombre.

¿Quién responde si la aduana detecta un error de clasificación?

Ante la autoridad responde el importador registrado, porque el pedimento se emite a su nombre. Cómo se distribuye ese costo entre usted y el FIOR depende de lo que hayan pactado por contrato.

¿El FIOR resuelve también mi situación fiscal en Amazon?

No. Son dos cosas distintas. El FIOR resuelve la importación; la retención de Amazon depende de si usted proporcionó un RFC válido. Sin RFC la retención sigue siendo de 20 por ciento de ISR y del IVA completo.

¿Qué pasa con la Manifestación de Valor?

Es obligación del importador y desde el 1 de agosto de 2026 debe presentarse electrónicamente. El importador necesita que usted le entregue facturas y evidencia de pago que sustenten el valor declarado.

translations.title: Cómo Leer Un Pedimento Campo Por Campo
translations.excerpt: La mayoría de los importadores archiva el pedimento sin leerlo. Es el documento que la autoridad le pedirá en una revisión y el que determina si pagó de más o de menos.
translations.content:
El pedimento es la declaración aduanera oficial de una operación de comercio exterior en México. Se organiza en bloques: datos del importador y del agente aduanal, régimen y tipo de operación, datos del transporte, valor en aduana y su determinación, fracciones arancelarias por partida, y liquidación de contribuciones. Revíselo antes de que se archive: la clasificación arancelaria y el valor declarado son los dos campos que determinan cuánto pagó y qué tan expuesto está en una revisión posterior.

  • El pedimento es el registro legal de la operación y es lo que la autoridad solicita en cualquier revisión posterior al despacho.
  • La fracción arancelaria determina el arancel aplicable y también qué regulaciones no arancelarias se activan.
  • El valor en aduana no es sólo el precio de factura: incorpora incrementables como flete y seguro hasta el punto de entrada.
  • El IVA de importación se calcula sobre el valor en aduana más el impuesto general de importación, por lo que el arancel amplía la base.
  • Desde el 1 de agosto de 2026 la Manifestación de Valor que sustenta ese valor se presenta de forma electrónica obligatoria.

¿Qué bloques componen un pedimento?

Identificación de las partes, régimen aduanero, transporte, valor y su determinación, partidas con su fracción arancelaria, y la liquidación de contribuciones.

El pedimento parece denso porque lo es, pero está organizado por bloques y cada bloque responde a una pregunta. El bloque de identificación dice quién importa y quién despacha: el RFC del importador registrado y los datos del agente aduanal. Si el nombre del importador no es el que usted espera, deténgase ahí y pregunte. El bloque de régimen indica qué tipo de operación es: importación definitiva, temporal, retorno. El régimen cambia por completo las obligaciones posteriores, y una importación temporal mal cerrada se convierte en un problema fiscal meses después. El bloque de transporte registra el medio, el transportista y los datos del cruce. El bloque de valor es el más importante y el que menos gente lee. Contiene el valor en aduana, el valor comercial y los incrementables. El bloque de partidas desglosa la mercancía: cada partida lleva su descripción, su fracción arancelaria, cantidad y valor. Y el bloque de liquidación suma lo que se pagó: impuesto general de importación, IVA, DTA y cualquier otra contribución. Ese total debe cuadrar con lo que su agente le cobró. Si trabaja con un agente aduanal, pídale la guía de campos de su sistema. Cada uno numera los apartados conforme al formato vigente y es más útil revisar el suyo que memorizar un esquema genérico.

¿Qué debo revisar sí o sí?

La fracción arancelaria, la descripción de la mercancía, el valor en aduana y el régimen. Esos cuatro campos concentran casi todo el riesgo.

La fracción arancelaria es el campo que más dinero mueve. Determina el arancel, y también si su mercancía necesita permiso, NOM o inscripción en un padrón sectorial. Una fracción incorrecta no sólo cambia lo que paga: puede significar que importó sin un permiso que sí requería. La descripción debe corresponder con lo que realmente venía. Si el pedimento dice una cosa y la caja contiene otra, ese desfase es exactamente lo que se detecta en un reconocimiento aduanero. El valor en aduana debe ser sustentable con documentos. No es únicamente el precio de la factura: incorpora incrementables. Si su agente declaró un valor y usted no tiene cómo respaldarlo con orden de compra y evidencia de pago, tiene una contingencia abierta. El régimen determina qué le toca hacer después. Una importación temporal tiene plazo de retorno; si vence sin regularizarse, se convierte en una omisión. Un hábito que ahorra dinero: revise el pedimento el mismo día que lo recibe, no cuando llegue un requerimiento. Las rectificaciones son más baratas y más simples cuando se hacen a tiempo.

¿Qué errores salen más caros?

Clasificación incorrecta, valor sin sustento y régimen mal elegido. Los tres se detectan tarde y se corrigen caro.

La clasificación incorrecta es el error más común. A veces es a la baja, y entonces hay omisión de contribuciones. A veces es a la alta, y entonces pagó de más sin saberlo. En ambos casos, cuando la autoridad revisa, la diferencia se determina con actualizaciones y recargos. El valor sin sustento aparece cuando el precio declarado no puede documentarse. Aquí conviene ser claro: subvaluar no es una estrategia, es una contingencia. La autoridad tiene mecanismos para cuestionar valores que se apartan de lo esperado para esa fracción, y la carga de demostrar el valor de transacción es del importador. El régimen mal elegido suele venir de operaciones que se plantearon como temporales y terminaron siendo definitivas de facto. La mercancía se quedó, el plazo venció, nadie regularizó. Y hay un cuarto que ahora tiene fecha: la documentación de valor. Desde el 1 de agosto de 2026 la Manifestación de Valor debe presentarse electrónicamente por la ventanilla única que la ANAM denomina VUTCE en sus comunicados de 2026. Un expediente que no puede sustentar el valor declarado ya no sólo es débil ante una revisión: incumple una obligación con fecha cierta.

Los cuatro campos de mayor riesgo

CampoQué determinaSi está mal
Fracción arancelariaArancel, permisos, NOM, padrón sectorialOmisión de contribuciones o importación sin permiso
Descripción de mercancíaCorrespondencia con lo físicoDiscrepancia en reconocimiento aduanero
Valor en aduanaBase de arancel e IVARevisión de valor, determinación con recargos
Régimen aduaneroObligaciones posterioresTemporal vencida convertida en omisión

Definiciones

  • Incrementables: Los incrementables son los conceptos que se suman al precio pagado para determinar el valor en aduana, como el flete y el seguro hasta el punto de entrada.
  • Rectificación: La rectificación es la corrección formal de un pedimento ya presentado, y es más simple y barata cuanto antes se realice.

Preguntas frecuentes

¿Quién me entrega el pedimento?

Su agente aduanal, como parte del despacho. Consérvelo: es el documento que la autoridad solicitará en cualquier revisión posterior a la operación.

¿El valor en aduana es el precio de mi factura?

No necesariamente. Parte del precio pagado e incorpora incrementables como flete y seguro hasta el punto de entrada, por lo que suele ser mayor que el valor de factura.

¿Sobre qué se calcula el IVA de importación?

Sobre el valor en aduana más el impuesto general de importación y, en su caso, otras contribuciones. El arancel amplía la base del IVA.

¿Puedo corregir un pedimento ya presentado?

Sí, mediante rectificación. Tiene costo y puede implicar demora, pero es considerablemente más barato que esperar a que la autoridad detecte la diferencia.

translations.excerpt: İki teklif arasındaki fark genelde fiyat farkı değil, kapsam farkıdır. Ucuz görünen teklif çoğu zaman aynı işi kapsamıyordur.
translations.content:
Meksika gönderiminde teklifte genelde sadece navlun yazar. Faturaya eklenen kalemler şunlardır: gümrük müşavirlik ücreti, ithalat vergisi, yüzde 16 IVA, gümrük işlem hakkı, fiziki muayeneye düşerse muayene ve elleçleme masrafı, mal beklerse ardiye, pedimento düzeltmesi gerekirse rektifikasyon ücreti ve Meksika içi dağıtım. Teklifleri karşılaştırırken tek soru yeterli: bu fiyata neler dahil, neler değil.

  • IVA yüzde 16'dır ve gümrük değeri artı ithalat vergisi üzerinden hesaplanır; yani vergi, verginin matrahını da büyütür.
  • Gümrük müşavirlik ücreti vergiden ayrı bir hizmet bedelidir ve navlun teklifine dahil olmayabilir.
  • Türkiye USMCA üyesi olmadığı için Türk menşeli ürün tercihli tarifeden yararlanamaz; ABD deposunda beklemek bunu değiştirmez.
  • Fiziki muayene otomatik seçim mekanizmasıyla belirlenir; kimse muaf değildir ve masrafı ithalatçıya aittir.
  • Amazon Meksika'da RFC bildirmeyen satıcıdan yüzde 20 ISR stopajı ve IVA'nın tamamı kesilir; bu da bir maliyet kalemidir.

Teklifte ne yazar, faturada ne çıkar?

Teklifte genelde sadece taşıma yazar. Faturada müşavirlik, vergi, IVA, işlem hakkı ve varsa muayene, ardiye, düzeltme kalemleri de çıkar.

Bir Türk satıcının Meksika'ya ilk sevkiyatında en sık yaşadığı şey şudur: teklif makul görünür, fatura beklenenin epey üstünde gelir. Firma sizi kandırmamıştır çoğu zaman; teklif sadece navlunu kapsamıştır. Gerçek maliyet şu kalemlerden oluşur. Navlun, yani taşımanın kendisi. Gümrük müşavirlik ücreti, yani pedimentoyu hazırlayıp beyanı yapan müşavirin hizmet bedeli. İthalat vergisi, HS kodunuza ve menşeinize göre. IVA, yüzde 16. Gümrük işlem hakkı. Ve Meksika içi dağıtım. Sonra ihtimale bağlı kalemler geliyor: sevkiyatınız fiziki muayeneye düşerse muayene ve elleçleme masrafı, mal gümrükte beklerse ardiye, beyanda bir düzeltme gerekirse rektifikasyon ücreti. Bu kalemlerin hiçbiri gizli değil aslında. Sadece sorulmadığı için söylenmiyor. Teklif alırken tek bir soru bütün tabloyu değiştirir: *bu fiyata neler dahil, neler değil?*

En çok şaşırtan kalem: IVA'nın matrahı

IVA sadece mal bedeli üzerinden değil, gümrük değeri artı ithalat vergisi üzerinden hesaplanır. Vergi, verginin tabanını büyütür.

Çoğu satıcı IVA'yı fatura tutarının yüzde 16'sı diye hesaplar. Yanlış hesaplar. IVA, gümrük değeri artı ithalat vergisi üzerinden hesaplanır. Gümrük değeri de sadece mal bedeli değildir; navlun ve sigorta gibi kalemleri de içerir. Yani zincir şöyle işler: mal bedeli üstüne taşıma eklenir, gümrük değeri çıkar; üstüne ithalat vergisi eklenir; ve IVA bu toplamın üzerinden hesaplanır. Bunun pratik sonucu şu: ithalat vergisi oranı yükseldiğinde ödediğiniz fazladan tutar sadece o verginin kendisi değildir, IVA'nın da artışıdır. Burada Türk satıcıyı özellikle ilgilendiren bir nokta var. Türkiye USMCA tarafı olmadığı için Türk menşeli ürün tercihli tarifeden yararlanamaz; kendi tarife pozisyonunun genel oranını öder. ABD deposunda beklemek, etiketlemek veya yeniden paketlemek menşei değiştirmez. Fiyatlamanızı USMCA muafiyeti varmış gibi kurarsanız aradaki farkı marjınızdan karşılarsınız. Eğer Meksika'da kayıtlı mükellefseniz IVA sizin için nihai bir maliyet değil, mahsup edilebilir bir kalemdir. Kayıtlı değilseniz cebinizde kalır. Bu ayrım, yapıyı baştan doğru kurmanın en somut getirisidir.

Teklif alırken hangi soruları sormalıyım?

Kapsam, sınıflandırma, ihtimale bağlı kalemler ve kimin ithalatçı göründüğü. Dört soru yeterli.

Bu fiyata neler dahil? Navlun mu sadece, yoksa müşavirlik ve iç dağıtım da var mı? Gümrük vergisi ve IVA dahil mi, yoksa maliyete mi yansıtılacak? Malımı hangi HS koduyla sınıflandıracaksınız ve vergi oranı ne? Bunu sevkiyattan önce söyleyemeyen bir firmadan teklif almayın. Sınıflandırma vergiyi, izin gerekliliğini ve NOM zorunluluğunu belirler. Sonradan öğrenilen bir izin şartı, malın sınırda beklemesi demektir. Fiziki muayeneye düşersem ne olur, masrafı kime ait? Muayene otomatik seçimle belirlenir, kimse muaf değildir. Önemli olan bunun nasıl faturalandırılacağını önceden bilmektir. Kayıtlı ithalatçı kim görünecek? Meksika'ya ticari ithalatta kayıtlı ithalatçı RFC sahibi bir Meksika tüzel kişiliği olmak zorunda. Sizin adınıza kim görünüyorsa, beyanın doğruluğundan gümrüğe karşı o sorumludur. Bunu baştan netleştirin. Son olarak, teklifleri karşılaştırırken kalem kalem karşılaştırın. Toplam rakamları yan yana koymak yanıltır; ucuz görünen teklif çoğu zaman daha az iş kapsıyordur.

Maliyet kalemleri: kesin olanlar ve ihtimale bağlı olanlar

KalemKesin mi?Neye bağlı
NavlunKesinHacim, ağırlık, parsiyel/tam araç
Gümrük müşavirlik ücretiKesinİşlemin karmaşıklığı, kalem sayısı
İthalat vergisiKesinHS kodu ve menşe
IVA (%16)KesinGümrük değeri + ithalat vergisi

Ardiyeİhtimale bağlıGümrükte bekleme süresi

Tanımlar

  • Gümrük değeri: Gümrük değeri, verginin üzerinden hesaplandığı değerdir ve mal bedeline navlun ile sigorta gibi kalemlerin eklenmesiyle bulunur.
  • Rektifikasyon: Rektifikasyon, düzenlenmiş bir pedimentonun resmî olarak düzeltilmesidir; ücreti vardır ve genelde gecikmeye yol açar.

Sık sorulan sorular

Navlun teklifi neden gerçek maliyeti göstermiyor?

Çünkü navlun sadece taşımadır. Gümrük müşavirliği, ithalat vergisi, yüzde 16 IVA, işlem hakkı ve Meksika içi dağıtım ayrı kalemlerdir ve teklife dahil olmayabilir. Teklif alırken kapsamı açıkça sorun.

IVA'yı nasıl hesaplamalıyım?

Fatura tutarının yüzde 16'sı olarak değil. IVA, gümrük değeri artı ithalat vergisi üzerinden hesaplanır; gümrük değeri de navlun ve sigortayı içerir. Yani vergi, IVA'nın matrahını da büyütür.

Türk ürünüm USMCA sayesinde vergiden muaf mı?

Hayır. Türkiye USMCA tarafı değil. Ürün kendi tarife pozisyonunun genel oranını öder ve ABD deposunda beklemek menşei değiştirmez. Oran ürüne göre değişir, sınıflandırmadan sonra netleşir.

Fiziki muayeneden kaçınabilir miyim?

Hayır, seçimde rastlantısal bir bileşen var ve kimse muaf değil. Ancak doğru sınıflandırma, net mal tanımı ve tutarlı geçmiş hem seçilme olasılığını hem de seçildiğinizde geçen süreyi azaltır.

Ödediğim IVA'yı geri alabilir miyim?

Meksika'da kayıtlı mükellefseniz mahsup edebilirsiniz, yani nihai maliyet değil nakit akışı kalemidir. Kayıtlı değilseniz genelde geri alamazsınız ve doğrudan maliyet olarak kalır.

İlgili Yazılar

  • ABD'den Meksika'ya lojistiğin tamamı
  • doğru HS kodunu bulmak
  • gümrük müşaviri seçimi
  • Meksika'ya kargo gönderme yolları

translations.title: Meksika E-İhracatı: Türkiye'den Satışın Vergi Ve Lojistik Modeli
translations.excerpt: Meksika, Türk e-ihracatçısı için büyük ama yapısı zor bir pazar. Zorluk ürün ya da rekabet değil; ithalat yapısı ve vergi kurgusu.
translations.content:
Türkiye'den Meksika'ya e-ihracatta üç yapısal karar var: rota (doğrudan mı, ABD deposu üzerinden mi), ithalatçı yapısı (Meksika'da şirket, DDP satış veya kayıtlı ithalatçı hizmeti) ve vergi kaydı (RFC olup olmaması). Türk menşeli ürün USMCA'dan yararlanamaz, kendi tarife pozisyonunun genel oranını öder. Amazon Meksika'da RFC bildirmeyen satıcıdan yüzde 20 ISR ve IVA'nın tamamı kesilir.

  • Türkiye USMCA tarafı değildir; Türk menşeli ürün tercihli tarifeden yararlanamaz ve ABD'de depolanması menşei değiştirmez.
  • Meksika'ya ticari ithalatta kayıtlı ithalatçının RFC sahibi bir Meksika tüzel kişiliği olması ve ithalatçı siciline kayıtlı olması gerekir.
  • Amazon Meksika'da RFC bildirilmediğinde satış bedeli üzerinden yüzde 20 ISR stopajı ve yüzde 16 IVA kesintisi uygulanır.
  • IVA yüzde 16'dır ve gümrük değeri artı ithalat vergisi üzerinden hesaplanır.
  • Meksika'da tüketiciye satışta garanti süresi kanunen altmış günden az olamaz (Tüketicinin Korunması Kanunu md. 77).

Hangi rota: doğrudan mı, ABD üzerinden mi?

Doğrudan hat sınırlı ve pahalı. Pratikte kullanılan yol ABD deposunda konsolide edip kara sınırından geçmek.

Türkiye'den Meksika'ya doğrudan ticari taşıma seçenekleri sınırlı ve birim maliyeti yüksek. Bu yüzden hacimli satış yapan Türk satıcıların çoğu ABD üzerinden gidiyor: mal Türkiye'den ABD'ye geliyor, Teksas'ta bir depoda konsolide ediliyor, oradan kara sınırından Meksika'ya geçiyor. Bu rotanın somut avantajları var. Toplu geçiş sipariş bazlı gönderiden ucuz. Meksika içi teslimat süresi kısalıyor. ABD deposu iade adresi olarak kullanılabiliyor. Ve Amazon Meksika'ya FBA gönderimi bu yapıyla çok daha yönetilebilir hale geliyor. Dikkat edilmesi gereken nokta şu: bu rotada iki ayrı ithalat var. Malı ABD'ye soktuğunuzda bir ithalat, ABD'den Meksika'ya soktuğunuzda ikinci bir ithalat yapıyorsunuz. Her ikisinin kendi beyanı, kendi vergisi ve kendi belge seti var. ABD deposu bir ara durak değil, ayrı bir gümrük işlemidir. Maliyet modelinizi iki ithalat üzerinden kurun. Tek ithalat varsayıp hesap yapan satıcılar farkı marjdan karşılıyor.

İthalatçı yapısını nasıl kuracağım?

Üç seçenek: Meksika'da şirket kurmak, Meksikalı alıcıya DDP satmak, veya kayıtlı ithalatçı hizmeti almak.

Meksika'ya ticari ithalatta kayıtlı ithalatçının RFC sahibi bir Meksika mükellefi olması zorunlu. Türkiye'deki şirketiniz bu şartı sağlayamaz. Üç yolunuz var. Meksika'da şirket kurmak tam kontrol verir: kendi adınıza ithalat yaparsınız, IVA'yı mahsup edersiniz, Amazon stopajı normal rejime döner. Karşılığında aylar süren bir kuruluş süreci ve süreklilik arz eden vergi yükümlülükleri gelir — işlem olmasa bile beyanname verilir. Meksikalı alıcıya DDP satmak en basitidir. Müşteriniz kendi adına ithal eder. Ama gümrük sürecinin kontrolünü kaybedersiniz ve bu model B2C'de işlemez. Kayıtlı ithalatçı hizmeti e-ticaret satıcılarının çoğunun kullandığı yol. Bir Meksika tüzel kişiliği sizin adınıza ithalatçı olarak görünür. Amazon'un yabancı satıcıdan istediği FIOR budur. Meşru ve yaygın bir yapı, ama gerçek bir hukuki ilişki: kayıtlı ithalatçı beyanın doğruluğundan gümrüğe karşı sorumludur. Sözleşmede kimin neyi üstlendiğini netleştirin. Hangisini seçerseniz seçin, kararı sevkiyattan önce verin. Yapı kurulmadan yola çıkan mal sınırda bekler.

Vergi tarafı: RFC neden bu kadar önemli?

RFC yoksa Amazon satış bedeli üzerinden yüzde 20 ISR ve yüzde 16 IVA keser, ve kesilen IVA genelde geri alınamaz.

Bu, Meksika e-ihracatının en sert kalemi ve çoğu satıcı ilk hakediş raporunu görene kadar farkına varmıyor. RFC bildirmeyen satıcıdan Amazon Meksika iki kesinti yapıyor: yüzde 20 ISR stopajı ve IVA'nın tamamı, yani yüzde 16. İkisi de satış bedeli üzerinden hesaplanıyor, kâr üzerinden değil. Yüzde 15 marjla çalışan bir satıcı, yüzde 20 ISR ödediğinde marjının tamamından fazlasını o işlemde kaybediyor. RFC'niz varsa iki şey değişir. ISR stopajı rejiminize uygun orana düşer. Ve kesilen IVA mahsup edilebilir hale gelir — yani kalıcı bir maliyet olmaktan çıkıp nakit akışı kalemine dönüşür. Kayıtlı olmayan yabancı satıcı için kesilen IVA genelde geri alınamaz; sessizce kalıcı bir yüzde 16'dır. Bir de satış sonrası yükümlülük var: Meksika'da tüketiciye satışta garanti süresi kanunen altmış günden az olamaz (Tüketicinin Korunması Kanunu md. 77). İade ve garanti sürecinizi buna göre kurun; iade adresi olarak ABD deposu kullanmak burada işinizi kolaylaştırır. Pratik öneri: bir SKU alın, satış fiyatına yüzde 20 ISR ve yüzde 16 IVA uygulayın, üzerinden teslim maliyetini, Amazon komisyonunu ve karşılama ücretini düşün. Kalan rakam sizin gerçek Meksika iş modelinizdir — brüt marj değil.

Üç ithalatçı yapısının karşılaştırması

YapıKurulum süresiIVA mahsubuKime uygun
Meksika'da şirketAylarVarYüksek hacim, uzun vade
DDP satışHemenAlıcıdaB2B, yapısı hazır alıcılar
Kayıtlı ithalatçı hizmetiGünler-haftalarYapıya bağlıE-ticaret ve Amazon satıcıları

Tanımlar

  • RFC: RFC, Meksika vergi kimlik numarasıdır ve ithalat kaydı, fatura düzenleme ve düşük platform stopajı için gereklidir.
  • ISR stopajı: ISR stopajı, pazaryerinin satıcı hakedişinden kestiği gelir vergisidir ve satıcının vergi kaydı durumuna göre oranı değişir.

Sık sorulan sorular

Türkiye'den Meksika'ya doğrudan mı göndermeliyim, ABD üzerinden mi?

Hacimli satışta pratikte ABD üzerinden gidiliyor: Teksas'ta konsolide edip kara sınırından geçmek birim maliyeti düşürüyor ve teslim süresini kısaltıyor. Ancak bu rotada iki ayrı ithalat olduğunu ve her ikisinin kendi vergisi bulunduğunu hesaba katın.

Türk ürünüm Meksika'ya gümrüksüz girer mi?

Hayır. Türkiye USMCA tarafı değil, dolayısıyla tercihli tarife uygulanmaz. Ürün kendi tarife pozisyonunun genel oranını öder. ABD deposunda beklemek, etiketlemek veya yeniden paketlemek menşei değiştirmez.

RFC almadan Amazon Meksika'da satabilir miyim?

Satabilirsiniz ama satış bedeli üzerinden yüzde 20 ISR ve yüzde 16 IVA kesilir, ve kayıtlı olmayan yabancı satıcı kesilen IVA'yı genelde geri alamaz. Düşük marjlı üründe bu, marjın tamamını aşabilir.

Meksika'da tüketiciye karşı garanti yükümlülüğüm ne?

Tüketicinin Korunması Kanunu'nun 77. maddesine göre garanti süresi, malın tesliminden itibaren altmış günden az olamaz. Bu yasal asgari süredir ve mağaza politikasıyla kısaltılamaz.

Meksika'da şirket kurmam şart mı?

Şart değil. Kayıtlı ithalatçı hizmeti alarak yerel şirket kurmadan ithalat yapabilirsiniz. Ancak IVA mahsubu ve düşük stopaj için vergi kaydı gerekiyor; hangi yapının size uygun olduğunu hacminize göre değerlendirin.

  • gümrük müşaviri nasıl seçilir

translations.title: How US To Mexico Cross-Border Shipping Works: The Complete Guide
translations.excerpt: Cross-border shipping to Mexico follows a clear sequence: export, border transfer, customs clearance and delivery. This guide walks through every step, with real times and costs.
translations.content:
Cross-border shipping from the US to Mexico works in five steps: your goods leave a US warehouse, US export is completed, a transfer tractor moves the trailer across the border, a licensed broker files the pedimento and pays duty and IVA, and the goods are released for delivery. With complete paperwork, clearance at Laredo is usually same day and delivery to Monterrey takes 1 to 2 business days. Commercial imports require a Mexican RFC and a customs broker.

  • A licensed customs broker (agente aduanal) must file the pedimento; since January 2025 every import declaration requires the importer of record's RFC (trade.gov).
  • Import IVA is 16 percent (SAT, trade.gov).
  • US origin goods enter at 0 percent duty on most products under the USMCA; goods from countries without a treaty face higher tariffs under the 2026 decree.
  • A well documented full truckload from Laredo reaches Monterrey in 1 to 2 business days (BringGo Ship operations data).
  • Laredo is North America's busiest inland port, with more than 17,000 trucks crossing per day (City of Laredo, 2026).

How does cross-border shipping from the US to Mexico work?

It is a chain of five steps that connects a US warehouse to a Mexican destination: export from the US, transfer across the border, customs clearance in Mexico, release, and domestic delivery.

Cross-border shipping is not one movement but a coordinated sequence. Your goods leave a US warehouse, ideally after the documents have been checked. US export formalities are completed on the American side. A transfer tractor then moves the trailer to the Mexican side of the border, a short step known as transfer or drayage. There, a licensed customs broker files the pedimento, the official import declaration, and pays the duty and IVA. Mexican customs assigns a green or red light, and once the goods are released, a domestic carrier takes them to their destination, such as Monterrey. Most of this traffic runs through Laredo because it is North America's busiest inland port. An operator with warehouses on both sides of the border can run the whole chain from one place: BringGo Ship works this model from its Laredo and Monterrey warehouses with a licensed customs broker.

What are the steps, from the US warehouse to a Mexican doorstep?

Five: leave the US warehouse, complete US export, transfer across the border, clear the pedimento in Mexico, and deliver domestically.

Seeing the shipment as steps makes it clear where a load can stall. First, the goods leave the US warehouse; this is the moment to confirm the invoice, packing list, and classifications. Second, US export formalities are completed on the American side. Third, the transfer or drayage tractor physically moves the trailer into Mexico. Fourth, the customs broker transmits and clears the pedimento, paying duty and IVA; at this point customs decides the light. Fifth, the released goods move by domestic transport to their final destination. Each step depends on the one before it, so an incomplete document in step one becomes a delay in step four. That is why a document review before the freight leaves the warehouse is the best use of time in the entire process.

What documents do you need to ship to Mexico?

Five core documents: commercial invoice, packing list, correct HS codes, certificate of origin for the USMCA rate, and the Complemento Carta Porte for the Mexican road leg.

The shipment rests on a consistent set of documents. The commercial invoice sets the value and description; the packing list details the contents per pallet with weights and dimensions; the HS codes (tariff classification) determine the duty and must be correct, because a wrong code raises inspection risk. The certificate of origin is what earns the USMCA preferential rate, and in 2026 it must be uploaded digitally before the shipment; if it is missing, you pay the full third country duty. The Complemento Carta Porte is required for road transport inside Mexico. The rule that prevents most delays is simple: the invoice, packing list, and pedimento must say exactly the same thing in value, quantity, and description.

How long does cross-border shipping to Mexico take?

With complete paperwork, clearance is usually same day and delivery to Monterrey takes 1 to 2 business days. Interior points add 2 to 4 days, and a red light adds 1 to 2 days.

Transit time is driven by customs, not distance. The Laredo infrastructure is fast because of its volume, so documentation is what makes the difference. With complete, consistent papers, clearance is usually same day and the goods reach Monterrey in 1 to 2 business days. For interior destinations like Mexico City, add 2 to 4 days of domestic transport. If the load draws a red light (rojo), physical inspection adds 1 to 2 days. Season matters too: around El Buen Fin in November and the December peak, the bridge and customs get busier, so leave a 2 to 3 day buffer. How much does it cost to ship to Mexico?

The fiscal cost combines the broker fee, duty, and IVA, plus freight. IVA is 16 percent; duty is 0 percent on most US origin goods under the USMCA.

The landed cost of a shipment has a few parts. The customs broker fee runs roughly 3,500 to 15,000 MXN per operation, or about 0.35 to 0.65 percent of value. Import IVA is 16 percent. Duty depends on origin: US origin goods enter at 0 percent on most products under the USMCA. A 2026 point to note: the decree effective January 1 raised tariffs to between 10 and 50 percent on about 1,648 tariff lines (1,463 plus 185 added in April 2026) for goods from countries without a treaty, such as China. There is also a de minimis for US origin goods under the USMCA: no tax up to 50 US dollars and no duty up to 117 US dollars. On top of the fiscal cost sits the freight itself. Because rates and rules shift, confirm the tariff for your product with your broker before each season.

Do you need a Mexican RFC and a customs broker?

For commercial imports, yes to both. Only a licensed broker can file the pedimento, and an RFC is required; if you lack one, an importer of record (IOR) lets you start.

Two requirements are non-negotiable for commercial importing. First, an RFC (the Mexican tax ID) and importer registration; since January 2025 every import declaration requires the importer of record's RFC, and the courier channel now asks for the consignee RFC as well. Second, a licensed customs broker (agente aduanal), because only a registered broker can file the pedimento. The 2026 reform added shared liability, so the importer and broker are jointly responsible for the declaration. If you do not yet have your own RFC, you can still ship through a partner that acts as the importer of record and clears the goods in its name while you complete your registration. This is a common way for a new seller to start selling into Mexico without waiting on paperwork.

Should you use LTL or FTL?

Roughly up to six pallets, less than truckload (LTL) is cheaper; for a full trailer, full truckload (FTL) is faster and clears on a single pedimento.

The choice comes down to volume. FTL means the trailer is yours: it moves on your schedule, crosses on a single pedimento, and is handled less, so there is less risk of damage or delay. For Laredo to Monterrey, a well documented FTL load usually arrives in 1 to 2 business days. LTL suits smaller volumes, roughly one to six pallets, where your freight shares the trailer with other shipments; that lowers the cost per pallet but adds consolidation time. A practical threshold: up to about six pallets, LTL is usually economical; a full trailer or an urgent, fragile load points to FTL. As your volume grows, moving to FTL tends to lower your per unit cost and speed up the border, so it is worth reviewing the mix regularly.

What are the most common mistakes that delay a shipment?

An invoice that does not match the pedimento, a wrong HS code, and a missing or late certificate of origin. All three are preventable before departure.

Most delays come from avoidable errors at the origin. The most common is an inconsistency between the invoice and the pedimento in value, quantity, or description, which triggers a hold. Next is an incorrect HS code, which changes the duty and raises the chance of a red light. Third, increasingly relevant in 2026, is failing to upload the certificate of origin digitally before shipment, which costs you the USMCA rate. Timing adds risk too: a trailer that reaches the border late on a Friday can sit through the weekend. Under the 2026 reform, the importer and broker share liability, so accuracy matters more than ever. The fix is always the same: verify every document while the freight is still at the warehouse, not at the bridge.

Frequently asked questions

How does cross-border shipping to Mexico work in simple terms?

Your goods leave a US warehouse, clear US export, a transfer tractor moves them across the border, a licensed broker clears the pedimento and pays duty and IVA, and a domestic carrier delivers them. With good paperwork, Laredo to Monterrey takes 1 to 2 business days.

Do I need a customs broker to ship to Mexico?

For commercial imports, yes. Only a registered agente aduanal can file the pedimento. You provide the invoice and product details; the broker classifies the goods, calculates duty and IVA, and transmits the declaration to the SAT.

Do I need a Mexican RFC?

How long does it take to ship from the US to Mexico?

With complete paperwork, clearance is usually same day and delivery to Monterrey takes 1 to 2 business days. Interior cities like Mexico City add 2 to 4 days, and a red light inspection adds 1 to 2 days.

How much duty will I pay?

US origin goods enter at 0 percent on most products under the USMCA, plus 16 percent IVA. In 2026, goods from countries without a treaty can pay 5 to 50 percent on about 1,648 tariff lines (1,463 plus 185 added in April 2026). Confirm your product's tariff with your broker.

What is the difference between LTL and FTL to Mexico?

LTL shares the trailer with other shipments and suits about one to six pallets, lowering cost per pallet but adding days. FTL is a dedicated trailer, faster and cleaner at the border, and better for full or urgent loads.

What is the biggest cause of delay?

A mismatch between the commercial invoice and the pedimento, followed by a wrong HS code. Both are prevented by checking the documents before the freight leaves the warehouse rather than at the border.
